 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  This is the time set aside for members of the public to address the City Council on
  items of interest that are not on the Agenda, but are within the subject matter
  jurisdiction of the San Gabriel City Council. Pursuant to the Brown Act, the City
  Council cannot answer any questions or take any action until such time as the
  matter may appear as an item on a future agenda.

  In an effort to provide everyone with an opportunity to speak tonight, please be
  aware that all public comments will be limited to a maximum of three minutes. I
  will give you a 30 second warning as you approach the end of your time. As a
  reminder, please be respectful of all speakers regardless of the position they take
  on any items.

  If you wish to address the City Council, please complete a speaker’s request card
  and hand it to me before the start of the meeting. When speaking, please state
  your NAME for the record.

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 15, 2019  2
   All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  This is the presentation of the “Register of Demands and Warrants” for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  B. INVESTMENT REPORT

  This is a presentation of City investments for the month of December 2018.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of December 18, 2018.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of December 18, 2018.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  D. AMENDED TOLLING AGREEMENT

  The Firefighters’ Association and its members have a tolling agreement with the
  City that permits them to preserve the affected firefighter employees’ wage-
  and-hour claims while the parties work toward a resolution of their dispute with
  the City without the costs of a lawsuit. The Firefighters’ Association would like
  to extend this agreement to facilitate settlement discussions.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the amended tolling
  agreement between the City of San Gabriel and the San Gabriel Firefighters’
  Association.

  E. RESOLUTION NO. 19-01 – ANNUAL RESOLUTION FOR TEMPORARY
  STREET CLOSURES DURING CITY EVENTS

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 15, 2019  3
   Each year, the City of San Gabriel hosts twelve street events in the Mission
  District and in San Gabriel Village. These festivals take place primarily along
  Mission Drive, Santa Anita Street, Broadway, and Fairview Avenue. To
  accommodate the events, as well as setup and cleanup, specific street segments
  must be closed to vehicular traffic.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution 19-01 (Attachment A)
  authorizing the Public Works Director to approve the specific street closures,
  dates and times for each event subject to the conditions stated in the
  Resolution No. 19-01.

  F. THEATER RENTAL FEE WAIVER REQUEST: ASIAN ARTS TALENTS
  FOUNDATION

  Asian Arts Talents Foundation (AATF) is planning a cultural performance to be
  held at the Mission Playhouse and has approached the City with the idea to
  hold this as a free event to promote Asian arts and culture through dance. There
  will be no tickets sold and no entrance fee, which will allow access to all who
  are interested. The event will be open to the general public from San Gabriel
  and surrounding areas.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approves AATF’s request to waive the
  theater rental fee of $3,630.00 for the rehearsal and performance of the
  upcoming free admission community performance on June 22, 2019.

  G. SAN GABRIEL FIRE STATIONS 51 AND 52 RESTROOM IMPROVEMENT
  PROJECT CHANGE ORDER

  In May 2018, Council awarded the construction contract to RT Contractor
  Corporation for the San Gabriel Fire Station 51 and 52 Restroom Improvement
  Project. The project consisted of remodeling two existing dormitory rooms and
  15 square feet expansion of existing Fire Station 51 and remodeling existing
  uni-sex restroom and 82 square feet addition of uni-sex / American Disability
  Act Restroom at Fire Station 52.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 15, 2019  4
   1. Authorize the City Manager to execute the attached Change Order for Fire
  Station 51 and 52 with RT Contractor Corporation for the San Gabriel Fire
  Station 51 and 52 Restroom Improvement Project; and

  2. Approve a purchase order in the amount of $45,000.00 for a total contract
  amount of $243,000.00.

  H. REQUEST FOR A REIMBURSEMENT AGREEMENT FROM CONSOLIDATED
  FIRE PROTECTION DISTRICT OF LOS ANGELES COUNTY

  In 2014, the San Gabriel Fire Department entered into a three city agreement
  for fire management services with San Marino and South Pasadena Fire
  Departments as an innovative way to share costs and services and still provide
  the best service possible. In 2017, that agreement was dissolved. In April of
  2018, a Standards of Coverage and Deployment Study was completed by a third
  party consultant and presented to the Council. In the April presentation, service
  delivery models were discussed including a Feasibility Study from the
  Consolidated Fire Protection District of Los Angeles County (LAFCO). A
  Feasibility Study was completed in September of 2018. The Feasibility Study
  was presented to Council on December 19, 2018.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Make a motion to reallocate $18,000.00 from account 122-761-15-97-315
  to account 122-761-15-96-809; and

  2. Enter into a Reimbursement Agreement for the surveying of fire department
  facilities, equipment and vehicles with the Consolidated Fire Protection
  District of Los Angeles County.

  I. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH AECOM TO CONDUCT AN
  ECONOMIC ANALYSIS AND MARKET STUDY

  Creating a thriving business district in the City’s historic Mission District is a San
  Gabriel City Council priority. The purpose of a comprehensive economic
  analysis and market study is to identify and evaluate current and future
  commercial development opportunities in order to help the City to prioritize
  potential development opportunities in the Mission District. Further, potential
  developers interested in investing in the Mission District will benefit from the
  data as development scenarios derived from the study will provide valuable

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 15, 2019  5
   insight on whether a potential project will sustain future market conditions.
  Moreover, the City will benefit from knowing how to capitalize on the existing
  cultural assets such as the Mission Playhouse and San Gabriel Mission.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council Authorize the City Manager to execute
  the professional services agreement with AECOM to conduct a comprehensive
  economic analysis and market study for the Mission District.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. RESOLUTION NO. 19-02: PROPOSED FY 2019-2020 CDBG PROGRAM AND
  BUDGET PLAN

  The City receives Federal Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds
  from the Community Development Commission of the County of Los Angeles
  (CDC). The funds must be used to meet national objectives and to serve a low-
  and moderate-income population. Use of these federal funds also requires
  compliance with statutory requirements including financial, environmental
  review, procurement, construction, eligibility, reporting, and citizen
  participation.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt the attached Resolution No. 19-02 authorizing the allocation of
  CDBG Funds for the FY 2019-20 from the CDC for activities and projects
  described above and in Exhibit A of the Resolution;

  2. Carry over any CDBG funds unspent at the close of FY 218-19 and recognize
  the receipt of the FY 2019-20 CDBG Program funds awarded by the CDC to
  the City in the City FY 2018-19 Budget;

  3. Recognize the receipt of approximately $20,630 of CDBG funds from
  Supervisor Barger, if funds are approved by the Board of Supervisors for the
  After School Program;

  4. Allocate any FY 2019-20 CDBG funds greater than the estimated funds to
  the Public Facilities Elevator Modernization Project, Ramp and Sidewalk
  Improvement Project and/or the Youth Program; and

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 15, 2019  6
   5. Authorize the City Manager to execute new contracts with the CDC for the
  allocation of FY 2018-19 CDBG Program and make adjustments as necessary
  to reflect the actual allocation of funds to San Gabriel.

 6. NEW BUSINESS

  A. ORDINANCE NO. 650 REVISING THE COMPOSITION OF THE DESIGN
  REVIEW COMMISSION – INTRODUCTION

  During the interview process for commissioners in May 2018, Council Members
  expressed an interest in increasing the number of members on the Design
  Review Commission from three to five, and allowing for greater flexibility in
  appointing members from a range of professional skill sets which relate to
  Commission duties.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Waive full reading, read by title only, and introduce for first reading
  Ordinance No. 650 Revising the Composition of the Design Review
  Commission; and

  2. Direct the City Clerk to assign two-year terms for appointees so that term
  expirations are staggered.

  B. SPEED HUMP IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATION

  During the past year, residents of Country Club Drive between Hermosa Drive
  and Roses Road have requested that the City install traffic calming speed
  bumps on their street to slow down traffic and discourage cut-through traffic
  between Del Mar Avenue and Las Tunas Drive. The Public Works Department
  has not installed speed humps on City streets before due to performance
  concerns and a lack of budgeted funds. The Country Club Drive residents have
  offered to pay for the installation of speed humps on their street segment and
  they are asking the City to consider adopting a policy for implementation of
  speed humps.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff requests that the City Council consider speed hump implementation for
  residential streets and provide direction to staff.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 15, 2019  7
   C. AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL REAUTHORIZING AND
  READOPTING THE CITY’S PUBLIC, EDUCATIONAL, AND GOVERNMENTAL
  ACCESS SUPPORT FEE

  In 2006, the California Legislature adopted the Digital Infrastructure and Video
  Competition Act (“DIVCA”). DIVCA authorizes cities to adopt an ordinance
  imposing a fee on state franchise holders to support PEG channel facilities. On
  November 4, 2008, the Council adopted Ordinance No. 580 C.S. to require
  state-franchised video service providers to pay the City a PEG fee of 1% of the
  video service provider’s gross revenue attributable to the City. Charter
  Communications collects the 1% PEG access fee from its subscribers and
  subsequently remits these fees to the City.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff requests that the City Council:

  1.  Introduce for first reading by title only Ordinance No. 649 of the City
  Council of the City of San Gabriel, California reauthorizing the fee on state-
  franchised video service providers to support public, educational, and
  governmental channel facilities;

  2. Waive further reading of Ordinance No. 649; and

  3. Schedule the second reading and adoption of Ordinance No. 649 for
  February 5, 2019.

 7. PUBLIC COMMENT

 8. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 9. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

 10. CLOSED SESSION – None.

 11. ADJOURNMENT

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – January 15, 2019  8
   The City Council will adjourn the meeting in memory of Helen (Elena) Ozorid,
  former dancer in the Mission Play and other McGroarty productions; at the San
  Gabriel Mission Playhouse, McGroarty’s home in Tujunga, and the Hollywood Bowl.

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, February 5, 2019 at
  6:30 p.m. in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel,
  California. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be
  available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

  B.  SPEED HUMP IMPLEMENTATION CONSIDERATION

  Presentation made by Principal Engineer Algis Marciuska.

  Mark Ewing, a resident who resides at Country Club Drive, stated that per a poll
  he conducted on his block, more than two- thirds of the residents are in favor
  of speed bumps. He also stated that he had interviewed a Fire Captain in the
  area who said there were no issues with a speed  hump; and that he had
  consulted a construction company that deals with roads for an estimate of the
  cost of constructing a speed hump. In closing, he stated that the residents are
  ready to divide the cost among themselves and pay to have one in place.

  Barbara Sohal, a resident who resides at Country Club Drive, stated that she has
  seen a lot of people speeding down the streets and it has made her afraid of
  walking her dog at night. She asked Council to consider alternatives to speed
  humps if it cannot be implemented as the ambiance of the street has been
  destroyed.

  Chuck Sances, a resident and member  of Grassroots  San Gabriel,  questioned

  why the City is discussing the issues of speed humps when not all residents are
  not in favor of them.  He indicated that all the major streets in the City are
  overcrowded causing drivers to use residential  streets;  stated that even  if

  residents have offered to pay for speed humps, they should not carry the
  burden of the cost; and commented that speed humps may cause traffic to be
  diverted and can cause traffic to be impacted on other streets.

  Following a discussion about the cost of speed humps, average speeds traveled,
  traffic light synchronization and timing, use of temporary speed humps, repairs
  of road,  and potential liability, the City Council provided direction to staff to
  prepare a policy addressing the Implementation of Street Humps.

  brought forward for all involved. She welcomed Fred Kokash from the Sheraton San

  Gabriel Los Angeles, representing the San Gabriel Chamber of Commerce.
